description: Cast alloy bulkhead lamp with a ribbed glass dome and a wire guard, over a shophouse door or stairwell

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small wall-mounted bulkhead light, an oval cast metal back plate lying flat against the wall with a thick moulded rim, a shallow ribbed glass dome bulging out of its centre, and over the dome a guard of a few thick flat metal straps arching from the rim across the face and meeting at the middle, a small screw boss at each end of the back plate Materials: Cream painted cast alloy gone yellow and chalky with paint flaking off the rim to bare metal, rust weeping from the screw bosses and running down the wall below, prismatic glass dome clouded with dust and grease and holding a dark drift of dead insects in its bottom, guard straps rust-pitted.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless white backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Final whole-asset visual estimate 95/100 for the procedural game prop, based on the same reference/render pair and full turntable. Rounded guard is genuinely welded: one component, zero boundary/non-manifold edges, four crossings; no self-intersection or sampled glass penetration. Remaining approximation is subtle glass scattering/reflectance and hidden rear detail, not a structural defect. 3492/3500 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 geometries. Factory about 46 ms; four textures about 1 MB. Standard PBR and imports only three.

featureReviews.notes: Circular flange, shallow dome and wall-normal projection match reference. Calibrated silhouette IoU .973; rear closed.
One connected watertight rounded cage with four welded crossings; no self intersections and no significant sampled glass penetration. Smooth vertically fluted glass; two moulded cast registers.
Cream paint, brown guard, gray-green frosted glass and plated screw heads distinct; source-derived chips/insect stain; all three material crop checks and material gate pass.
Closed planar rear at z=0, back-center root pivot; no extraneous mechanisms or sockets.

name: Bulkhead Wall Pack Light
nameTh: โคมไฟติดผนังกันน้ำ
notes:
Round cream-enamelled bulkhead light with a bowed four-bar guard built as one closed welded mesh, smooth vertically fluted pressed glass, and two plated cross-head fixings. Origin is back-center on the wall plane. Static wall fitting; physics stays disabled. The user-requested welded round guard supersedes the earlier flat-band construction.

SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-31, twice, both from measurement rather than estimate. (1) The FACE IS ROUND, not oval. A warm-pixel radial scan of the plate (the backdrop and its drop shadow are blue-grey at every level, so r > b separates fitting from ground) reads rH 422 px against rV 416.5 px, a ratio of 0.987; the declared 0.26 x 0.28 asserts 0.929. The width was right and the height was the estimate, so h 0.28 -> 0.26. (2) The PROJECTION was nearly double. The plate is head-on and carries no depth, so it comes from the Meshy proxy via scratch/_lights/axprof.mjs, which profiles radius against the proxy's own axis of revolution -- the axis of smallest extent, Meshy's orientation about every axis being arbitrary. Proxy extents are 1.8958 x 1.8950 x 0.7758, which confirms the round face a second time and gives w:d = 2.444; at w 0.26 that is a projection of 0.1064 m. The declared 0.19 would be a dome deeper than a hemisphere on a 0.26 m disc. d 0.19 -> 0.106.

Current medium scene budget: 3500 triangles, 2 draw calls, 2 materials, 4 unique geometries. The triangle ceiling was raised from 2000 to retain rounded welded sections, curved clearance above glass and moulded casting details; measured final costs are 3492 / 2 / 2 / 2. Existing Meshy evidence reused; no new paid generation.
